A **swimmer plot** gives one lane per patient: lane length = time on study, marker shapes = status at last follow-up (alive arrowhead, dead cross, lost asterisk), an open circle for progression, and a colour overlay for the duration of second-line therapy \[1\]. It is the standard companion to an oncology waterfall plot — response depth plus response *duration* in one figure. This tutorial reproduces the reference's base-graphics + `shape` recipe on 12 simulated patients:

## Example

![](../images/SwimmerPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="Swimmer Plot DEMO" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming language: R

-   Dependent packages: `shape`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shape))
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

12 patients with time on study (sorted ascending so the legends fit the empty corner), status at last follow-up, progression time, and a new-therapy overlay window. The reference's own warning is honoured: wrap every `PFS.time`/`Therapy_time` comparison in `!is.na()` to silence its "NAs introduced by coercion" noise:

```{r load data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shape))
set.seed(18601)
n <- 12
dat <- data.frame(
  ID = sprintf("P%02d", 1:n),
  OS.time = sort(round(runif(n, 4, 30), 1)),
  OS = sample(c("Alive", "Dead", "Missing"), n, TRUE, prob = c(0.55, 0.3, 0.15)),
  PFS.time = NA, PFS = "DS", New_therapy = sample(c("Yes", "No"), n, TRUE, prob = c(0.4, 0.6)))
dat$PFS.time <- round(dat$OS.time * runif(n, 0.25, 0.95), 1)
dat$PFS[dat$PFS.time > dat$OS.time] <- "DS"
dat$Therapy_time <- ifelse(dat$New_therapy == "Yes", round(dat$OS.time * runif(n, 0.1, 0.7), 1), NA)
dat <- dat[order(dat$OS.time), ]
rownames(dat) <- dat$ID
```

## Visualization

### 1. One Lane per Patient

The composite: blue lanes = time on study (sorted), yellow overlays = new-therapy duration, red arrowheads = alive at last contact, crosses = deaths, asterisks = lost to follow-up, open circles = progression — the JCO-style marker set on the reference's base-graphics frame:

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1Swimmer
#| fig-cap: "Swimmer plot of 12 simulated patients: blue lanes are time on study, yellow overlays new-therapy duration, red arrowheads mark patients alive at last follow-up, crosses deaths, asterisks lost to follow-up, and open circles progression."
#| out.width: "90%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shape))
jcoBlue <- "#248EC9"; jcoYellow <- "#EDC622"; jcoRed <- "#BE5D54"
par(bty = "o", mgp = c(1.5, .33, 0), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 2), las = 1, tcl = -0.25)
plot(NULL, NULL, xlim = c(0, max(dat$OS.time)) + max(dat$OS.time) / 3.2,
     ylim = c(0.5, nrow(dat) + 0.5), xlab = "Time on study (months)", ylab = "", yaxt = "n",
     main = "Swimmer plot: duration of response and status at last follow-up (simulated)")
axis(side = 2, at = seq_len(nrow(dat)), labels = rownames(dat), cex.axis = 0.75)
for (p in seq_len(nrow(dat))) {
  lines(c(0, dat[p, "OS.time"]), c(p, p), lwd = 9, col = jcoBlue)
  if (!is.na(dat[p, "Therapy_time"]))
    lines(c(dat[p, "Therapy_time"], dat[p, "OS.time"]), c(p, p), lwd = 9, col = jcoYellow)
  if (dat[p, "OS"] == "Alive")
    Arrows(dat[p, "OS.time"] + 0.2, p, dat[p, "OS.time"] + 1.4, p,
           arr.type = "triangle", arr.length = 0.22, arr.width = 0.22, lwd = 2, col = jcoRed)
  else if (dat[p, "OS"] == "Dead")
    points(dat[p, "OS.time"] + 0.9, p, pch = 3, lwd = 4, cex = 1.1, col = "grey20")
  else
    points(dat[p, "OS.time"] + 0.9, p, pch = 8, lwd = 3, cex = 1, col = "grey20")
  if (!is.na(dat[p, "PFS.time"]) && dat[p, "PFS"] == "DP")
    points(dat[p, "PFS.time"], p, pch = 21, lwd = 4, bg = "white", cex = 1.9, col = "grey10")
}
legend("bottomright", bty = "n", cex = 0.78, lwd = c(9, 9), col = c(jcoBlue, jcoYellow),
       legend = c("Time on study", "New therapy duration"), seg.len = 1.6)
legend("bottomright", inset = c(0, 0.16), bty = "n", cex = 0.78, pch = c(17, 3, 8, 21),
       pt.lwd = c(2, 4, 3, 4), col = c(jcoRed, "grey20", "grey20", "grey10"),
       legend = c("Alive (censored)", "Dead", "Lost to follow-up", "Progression"), pt.cex = 1.2)
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   Sort lanes **ascending by time on study** before drawing: the longest swimmer sits at the top, and the empty lower-right corner receives the legends.
-   Place legends at **computed data coordinates** (here the corner past `max(OS.time)`) — the reference hand-tunes fixed coordinates and then finishes in Illustrator.
-   Wrap every marker position in `!is.na()` — patients without progression or therapy produce `NA` x positions that would otherwise draw nothing but warn on every row.
:::

## Applications

::: {#fig-SwimmerApplications1}
![](../images/SwimmerPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="Patient-level treatment timeline" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

Patient-level treatment timeline
:::

Any per-patient timeline re-uses the lane grammar: CAR-T persistence with lymphodepletion overlay, pregnancy timelines with exposure windows, or device implantation with adverse-event markers.

## Reference

\[1\] Xiaofan Lu, et al. FigureYa: A Standardized Visualization Framework for Enhancing Biomedical Data Interpretation and Research Efficiency. iMetaMed. 2025. doi:10.1002/imm3.70005

\[2\] Chau I, et al. Nivolumab in previously treated patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (reference of the swim-plot style). J Clin Oncol. <https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/JCO.2017.76.9901>
